record.paper_title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?
record.context_brief: Phase-space transformations versus Einstein gauge transformations
record.original_question: Is the group of transformations generated in Hamiltonian phase space the same as, or at least inclusive of, the gauge-transformation group of Einstein General Relativity, including the diffeomorphism-type transformations of all gravitational variables such as g_{0μ} and the ADM lapse and shift variables?

evidence.quote: Is the group of transformation in phase space the same as the group of gauge transformation of the Einstein theory?

The same situation we face in gravitational theory: while the transformations of the 3-metrics can be generated by the secondary (momentum) constraints, the transformation for g_{0μ} cannot be obtained in this way.

In this case the group of transformation in phase space includes the group of gauge transformation of the Einstein theory, and we have an explicit prescription how to build up the generator of these transformations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein–Hilbert action for general relativity, viewed both in its Lagrangian (covariant) form, where the gauge group is the group of spacetime diffeomorphisms acting on the metric components $g_{\mu\nu}$ (including the components $g_{0\mu}$), and in its Hamiltonian (ADM) form, where one performs a $3+1$ decomposition introducing the lapse $N$, shift $N^i$, the spatial three-metric $h_{ij}$, and their conjugate momenta. In the Hamiltonian formulation, first-class constraints (the Hamiltonian constraint and the momentum/diffeomorphism constraints) generate a group $G_{\rm phase}$ of transformations on phase space (e.g., via the Dirac or Castellani prescription combining primary and secondary first-class constraints with appropriate parameters).

Let $G_{\rm Einstein}$ denote the gauge group of the Einstein theory, namely the group of spacetime diffeomorphism-type transformations acting on all gravitational variables, including $g_{0\mu}$ and equivalently the lapse and shift $(N,N^i)$.

Determine whether $G_{\rm phase} = G_{\rm Einstein}$, or at least whether $G_{\rm phase} \supseteq G_{\rm Einstein}$. Equivalently: is there a construction of the canonical generator on phase space such that the induced transformations of all components $g_{\mu\nu}$ — in particular of $g_{0\mu}$ (the lapse and shift) — coincide with (or contain) those produced by the spacetime diffeomorphism group of the Lagrangian theory?
artifact.status_search_result: The relationship between phase-space (canonical) gauge transformations and Lagrangian diffeomorphisms in GR has been studied extensively (Castellani's algorithm, Pons–Salisbury–Shepley, Kiriushcheva–Kuzmin and others). It is known that with appropriate combinations of first-class constraints one can generate transformations that include the spacetime diffeomorphisms of all metric components, including $g_{0\mu}$ and the lapse/shift, though typically through field-dependent (lapse/shift-dependent) reparametrizations of the gauge parameters. Thus the question is partially settled: inclusion $G_{\rm phase}\supseteq G_{\rm Einstein}$ can be achieved, but full equality and the conceptual interpretation remain debated in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Gauge transformations in the Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formalisms of generally covariant theories
status_evidence.snippet: Pons, Salisbury, Shepley show how Castellani's algorithm yields canonical generators reproducing diffeomorphisms, with field-dependent gauge parameters depending on lapse and shift.
status_evidence.claim: Canonical gauge generators can reproduce diffeomorphism transformations of all metric components including g_{0μ}, but require field-dependent (lapse/shift-involving) parameters.

status_evidence.title: The Hamiltonian formulation of general relativity: myths and reality
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses whether the canonical phase-space gauge group of GR coincides with the diffeomorphism group, including transformation of g_{0μ}.
status_evidence.claim: The equivalence of the phase-space gauge group with the Einstein gauge group is a debated, only partially settled, question.

status_evidence.title: Reduced Phase Space Approach to the Einstein equations
status_evidence.snippet: The gauge group for generally covariant systems is larger than the original group of spacetime diffeomorphisms, since its generators must depend on the lapse and shift.
status_evidence.claim: Phase-space gauge group includes (and may extend) the diffeomorphism group acting on lapse/shift.
